prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1295; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver reporting a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Insured reports minor front-end damage to vehicle and states they experienced neck pain at the scene. Ambulance was not requested. Policy coverage confirmed as active. Claim file opened and assigned for review.

Entry 2: Contacted the other driver's carrier to confirm liability position. Police report obtained and reviewed; it notes both vehicles traveling at low speed and a disputed lane position. Photos of both vehicles received from the insured show consistent frontal damage. Preliminary liability assessment pending further statements.

Entry 3: Notice of representation received from the claimant's attorney. All further communication to be directed through counsel. Request for medical records and authorization forms sent to attorney's office. Claimant's vehicle inspected at repair facility; estimate reviewed and found to be in line with the reported impact severity.

Entry 4: Attorney's office provided initial treatment summary indicating claimant was seen at urgent care and diagnosed with cervical strain. Physical therapy referral noted. Records requested for prior neck complaints. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect documented soft-tissue injury and anticipated treatment course.

Entry 5: Follow-up with claimant's counsel scheduled to discuss treatment progress and records received to date. Insured driver's recorded statement reviewed and consistent with police report. File remains open pending receipt of complete medical documentation and liability determination. Next review set for the standard follow-up interval.
